Wright-Patterson, its contractors and the Miami Valley shops: SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 for Dayton NDT people

Wright-Patterson Air Force Base is the largest single-site employer in Ohio, with more than 38,000 military, civilian and contractor staff. It houses Air Force Materiel Command, the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center that buys and sustains aircraft, engines and munitions, and the Air Force Research Laboratory. That mix of research, acquisition and sustainment sends work to contractors across the Miami Valley, and to the machining, forging, casting and coating shops that make parts for engine and airframe programs. The questions below are the ones a Dayton candidate or employer is likely to have about which certification scheme applies.

I work for a defense contractor near the base. Which document certifies me?

Usually the one your company's customer wrote into the contract. On defense aerospace programs, primes commonly pass NAS 410 down to their contractors, because NAS 410 replaced the old MIL-STD-410 that defense buying once relied on. Once a purchase order or quality clause invokes it, its minimums are mandatory and an auditor treats a shortfall as a nonconformance. The same contractor may hold other work, such as ground equipment, test fixtures or facility piping, under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A because the governing code calls for it. Ask your Level 3 which standard and which revision sit behind your certification letter, and keep a copy.

Does a private-sector NDT certification carry into a job on the base itself?

Not directly. Government positions follow federal hiring rules and the Air Force's own technical requirements, and people working on the installation work under their service's directives and the terms of their contracts. A certification issued by a private employer, under either scheme, ends when that employment ends. What you carry from one job to the next is evidence: course outlines with recorded hours, a signed experience log, your examination history and a current vision record. Whoever hires you next decides what that evidence is worth.

I do research or test support at a lab. Do I need either one?

Research and test work around the Air Force Research Laboratory and the University of Dayton Research Institute is governed by the contract and the test plan, not by the label on the building. Some tasks name a personnel standard; others do not. If yours does, that document applies in full. If the results will feed a flight-hardware decision, expect the customer to want traceable qualification, and ask early rather than after the report is written.

I am a machinist at a Miami Valley supplier moving into penetrant. What changes?

If the shop ships to an engine or airframe customer that invokes NAS 410, you will be certified under the shop's NAS 410 written practice, approved by its Responsible Level 3 (RL3). The RL3 decides what earlier training and experience to credit. An SNT-TC-1A certificate counts as evidence but does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement by itself. Penetrant and magnetic particle are the methods where NAS 410 sets heavier formal training demands than the SNT-TC-1A recommendations, so plan for the hours your RL3 sets before your first examination. The aerospace magnetic particle guide and penetrant testing training page show what the work covers.

Our small shop just received its first purchase order invoking NAS 410. Where do we start?

  1. Designate a Responsible Level 3 in writing. It can be an employee or a Level 3 supplied by an outside agency; the US has no national aerospace board to lean on, so the RL3 carries the program.
  2. Write or revise the NAS 410 written practice to Revision 6, released in December 2025, and keep it apart from any SNT-TC-1A program you already run.
  3. Rebuild each inspector's file so training, experience, examinations and vision can be traced from any signed report.
  4. Check whether the customer also requires Nadcap AC7114 accreditation for the methods you perform.

Atlantis provides NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit documentation support: we prepare and review the records and documents, and your RL3 approves them. Our aerospace audit support covers the SNT-TC-1A side.

Where Atlantis fits for Dayton

Three Atlantis services fit the Dayton market. Training on ASNT SNT-TC-1A combines self-paced online theory, answers from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) and the Practical NDT simulator, and finishes with hands-on work and the practical examination at the employer's site under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Dayton. Level III consulting gives contractors SNT-TC-1A-based aerospace written practices tied to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, procedures, Level I and II examinations and an outside agency Level III. Audit documentation support, described above, covers the records. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Dayton contractors or suppliers. A Miami Valley employer's RL3 alone decides whether outside coursework counts toward a NAS 410 certification; ask that question before you sign up. The side-by-side comparison of NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 explained give the background.
